title: Error logs causing disk leak
body:
### Tested versions

4.4-stable

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS

### Issue description

When an error is pushed in Godot, by default it gets appended to `/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/{game name}/logs/godot.log`. This file has no size limit so it just grows and grows. In C#, it's even worse because the entire stack trace is logged which results in a lot of data being appended. So if you throw an exception every frame, this will result in approximately 30kB being leaked every second, or 1GB every 10 hours. For client-side games this doesn't matter much, but for server-side dedicated servers, which often run for weeks/months at a time, this can be a big issue. Not just because certain errors can be harmless but also because it could be a security flaw.

### Steps to reproduce

Push an error every frame and check the user data logs folder. Watch it grow!

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[logs-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20219547/logs-test.zip)
